info.title: Tiducto Transit API — Realtime
info.description: GTFS-RT live data (vehicles, delays, alerts), poll-based and key-authenticated. Companion to routing and stops; the three share one pack version. A member that has no value is absent, never null. A GTFS-RT enum value the decoder doesn't recognise is omitted. Every id in a response is feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`), exactly as routing's `gtfsId` and stop search return it, and an id in a request is used exactly as sent: a raw id, or one with another feed's prefix, is unknown. A query parameter not listed is a 400 `<name> is not allowed`, and a repeated one a 400 `<name> is invalid`. A method an operation doesn't take is a 405 `method_not_allowed`, `POST /realtime/v1/delays` included, and a path under `/realtime/v1/` that matches no operation is a 404 `not_found`. A response may come from a shared cache keyed by host, URL and `apikey`; such a response is not metered. Any other path that matches no operation, and every path of an environment without a realtime deployment, is the gateway's plain-text `404 Not Found`, outside every operation.

servers.description: Your environment. Replace `{env-slug}` with your environment's slug.

get.description:
Live vehicle positions for the given trips, at most one per trip.
- `tripIds` is required: 1 to 50 comma-separated trip ids, each used exactly as sent and counted as sent. Absent or empty is a 400 `tripIds is required`, a blank entry (as in `1:39822,` or a space) a 400 `tripIds is invalid`, more than 50 a 400 `tripIds is out of range`.
- Ids are feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`), exactly as routing returns them; a raw id or another feed's id is unknown and listed in `missing`.
- A query parameter not listed is a 400 `<name> is not allowed`, and a repeated one a 400 `<name> is invalid`.
- The response carries `ETag`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<poll interval>, must-revalidate` and `Vary: apikey`; a request whose `If-None-Match` matches the `ETag` is a 304 without a body.

parameters.name: tripIds
parameters.description: 1 to 50 comma-separated feed-prefixed trip ids (`<feedId>:<id>`), each used exactly as sent (never trimmed) and counted as sent. Absent or empty is a 400 `tripIds is required`, a blank entry (as in `1:39822,` or a space) `tripIds is invalid`, and more than 50 ids `tripIds is out of range`.

200.description: Positions found, plus feed freshness; a requested id with no live vehicle, an unknown one included, is listed in `missing`.

ETag.description: The snapshot's entity tag; absent until the feed has reported.

Cache-Control.description: `public, max-age=<the feed's poll interval in seconds>, must-revalidate`; `public, max-age=5` until the feed has reported.

Vary.description: `apikey`: a shared cache keys the response by host, URL and `apikey`.

400.description: `tripIds` absent or empty is `tripIds is required`, a blank entry `tripIds is invalid`, and more than 50 ids `tripIds is out of range`. A query parameter not listed is `<name> is not allowed`, and a repeated one `<name> is invalid`; `field` names it.

401.description: The `apikey` header is missing (`key_missing`) or holds no valid key (`key_invalid`).

403.description: The key is not allowed on this operation (`key_not_allowed`), or the agreement it belongs to is inactive (`agreement_inactive`).

429.description: The key's rate limit is reached (`rate_limited`).

Retry-After.description: Seconds until a request is admitted again.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests the key may make per rate-limit window.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix seconds at which the rate-limit window resets.

4XX.description: Another client error: 404 `not_found`, 405 `method_not_allowed`, 411 `length_required` (a body without a length) or 413 `payload_too_large`.

5XX.description: From Spider, an ErrorResponse: `internal_error`, `upstream_unavailable` or `upstream_timeout`. A network intermediary in front of Spider may answer a 5XX with a body that is not JSON.

get.description:
Live schedule deviation for trips on one service date, resolved per trip instance (trip id + service date).
- `serviceDate` is the GTFS service date, ISO-8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`: the same value a plan leg's, departure's or trip's `serviceDate` carries. GTFS times may exceed 24:00, so a service date can differ from the departure's calendar date.
- `serviceDate` and `tripIds` are required; absent or empty is a 400 `<name> is required`.
- `tripIds` is 1 to 50 comma-separated trip ids, each used exactly as sent and counted as sent. A blank entry (as in `1:39822,` or a space) is a 400 `tripIds is invalid`, more than 50 a 400 `tripIds is out of range`.
- Ids are feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`), exactly as routing returns them; a raw id or another feed's id is unknown and listed in `missing`.
- A query parameter not listed is a 400 `<name> is not allowed`, and a repeated one a 400 `<name> is invalid`. Another method, `POST` included, is a 405 `method_not_allowed`.
- A trip instance the feed doesn't hold for that service date comes back in `missing`, never painted with another day's delay.
- The response carries `ETag`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<poll interval>, must-revalidate` and `Vary: apikey`; a request whose `If-None-Match` matches the `ETag` is a 304 without a body.

apikey.name: apikey
apikey.description: The raw key in an `apikey` header (not Authorization: Bearer).

missing.description: Requested trip ids with no live vehicle, exactly as sent.

feedTimestamp.description: Epoch seconds of the feed's latest report; absent when the feed has not reported.

staleSeconds.description: Seconds since `feedTimestamp`, as of when this body was produced; a cached or revalidated body keeps that value, and the age now is the current time minus `feedTimestamp`. Absent when `feedTimestamp` is.

vehicle.description: The trip's live vehicle; absent when none is reporting, a normal state rather than an error.

feedTimestamp.description: Epoch seconds of the feed's latest report; absent when the feed has not reported.

staleSeconds.description: Seconds since `feedTimestamp`, as of when this body was produced; a cached or revalidated body keeps that value, and the age now is the current time minus `feedTimestamp`. Absent when `feedTimestamp` is.

Vehicle.description: A vehicle's live position, at most one per trip. A member the producer doesn't report is absent. `tripId`, `routeId`, `stopId` and `vehicleId` are feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`).

label.description: The vehicle's user-visible label, as the producer gives it.

timestamp.description: Epoch seconds of the position; absent when the producer doesn't report it.

DelaysResponse.description: Delays for the requested service date. Feed freshness (`feedTimestamp`, `staleSeconds`) is global across the snapshot.

serviceDate.description: GTFS service date as ISO-8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`, echoing the request.

missing.description: Requested trip ids with no live delay on this service date, exactly as sent.

feedTimestamp.description: Epoch seconds of the feed's latest report; absent when the feed has not reported.

staleSeconds.description: Seconds since `feedTimestamp`, as of when this body was produced; a cached or revalidated body keeps that value, and the age now is the current time minus `feedTimestamp`. Absent when `feedTimestamp` is.

Delay.description: Live schedule deviation for one trip instance. A trip update without a start date applies to any requested service date; one with a start date applies to that date only. `tripId` and `routeId` are feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`).

delaySeconds.description: Seconds, positive when late: the delay of the last stop-time update that carries one, its departure delay before its arrival delay. Absent when the updates give only absolute times.

stopTimeUpdates.description: Empty when the update has none.

StopTimeUpdate.description: `stopId` is feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`). A member the producer doesn't set is absent.

arrivalDelay.description: Seconds, positive when late; absent when the update gives only an absolute arrival time.

departureDelay.description: Seconds, positive when late; absent when the update gives only an absolute departure time.

AlertsResponse.description: The alerts active now across the environment's feeds: inside any of their active periods, or always for an alert without one.

feedTimestamp.description: Epoch seconds of the feed's latest report; absent when the feed has not reported.

staleSeconds.description: Seconds since `feedTimestamp`, as of when this body was produced; a cached or revalidated body keeps that value, and the age now is the current time minus `feedTimestamp`. Absent when `feedTimestamp` is.

Alert.description: A service alert. Each text is the producer's first translation. A member the producer doesn't set is absent. `id` is feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`).

activePeriods.description: Empty for an alert that is always active.

ActivePeriod.description: A period the alert is active in; an absent `start` or `end` leaves that side open.

InformedEntity.description: What the alert concerns. Every id here is feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`); one the producer doesn't set is absent.

ErrorResponse.description: Error body: a stable machine-readable `code`, which names a state, and a human-readable `message`.

code.description: One of `bad_request`, `key_missing`, `key_invalid`, `key_not_allowed`, `agreement_inactive`, `planning_limit_reached`, `not_found`, `method_not_allowed`, `length_required`, `payload_too_large`, `rate_limited`, `internal_error`, `upstream_unavailable`, `upstream_timeout`. New codes may be added.

message.description: For `bad_request`: `<field> is required|invalid|out of range|not allowed`, or `body is invalid` when the body is empty, not JSON or not an object.

field.description: Present only on a 400 that names one member: its dot path from the body root, array positions omitted, or the query parameter's name.
